findings.claim: First-party Linux setup paths omitted the certutil provider package.
findings.evidence: Fresh setup could reach run_certutil without libnss3-tools or nss-tools; all owners and their tests now include the package.

findings.claim: The provider launch constructor dropped explicit clearCaCert.
findings.evidence: Provider clear serialized as omission before the amendment; the extracted builder now includes the shared transition helper.

findings.claim: The parsed connect launch envelope dropped clearCaCert and could trigger a separate local launch configuration.
findings.evidence: Both independent reviewers traced connect outside the four explicit builders; the new regression went red when parse_command stamping was removed.

findings.claim: Retained-CA rejection blamed a flag absent from the current invocation and omitted the clear remedy.
findings.evidence: The external-launch validation error now says CA trust is active for the session and instructs the user to pass --no-ca-cert.

findings.claim: Successful iOS and Safari provider launches returned before committing the resolved CA clear.
findings.evidence: The early branches now assign effective_ca_cert only after launch success.

findings.claim: MCP and Eve silently preferred CA set over simultaneous clear.
findings.evidence: Both adapters now reject the conflict and focused MCP/Eve tests pass.

findings.claim: The launch-envelope source-count test could stay green when production wiring was removed.
findings.evidence: A mutation removing real parsed-launch stamping left the original style of test green; the replacement drives parse_command and failed on the mutation.

findings.claim: External user snapshots created before this change can still lack nss-tools.
findings.evidence: Vercel and environments helpers accept arbitrary snapshot IDs and skip bootstrap for those snapshots; no local revision can invalidate a user-owned external snapshot.
